Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q2 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Klein, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Klein, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q2 earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Maxwell, CEO; Susan Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Alicia Rodriguez, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Maxwell, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our foundry business has seen significant traction with our 3GAP (Third Generation Advanced Performance) process node within the mobile application market. Specifically, we've secured design wins with seven new mobile application customers, a 40% increase compared to the five wins secured in Q1. This growth is a direct result of our focused efforts on optimizing 3GAP for low-power consumption and high-performance mobile applications, which are key differentiators in today's market.

We also continued to drive improvements through strategic management of our inventory. This quarter’s inventory position and associated DOI are a direct reflection of the proactive measures taken to mitigate ongoing global supply chain disruptions and the geopolitical instability. We anticipated and strategically secured key component inventory, particularly within the DX (Digital Experience) business unit, to ensure continuity of production and fulfillment despite these headwinds. This reflects our commitment to proactive risk management.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our revenue results, where we’ve delivered a strong Q2 2024 performance, achieving $77.2 billion in consolidated revenue. This marks the company's second-highest quarterly revenue on record and an all-time high for a second quarter, demonstrating resilience and growth in a complex global market.

Now I’ll hand it over to Susan to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Susan Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our CapEx, which reached $12.3 trillion this quarter, has contributed meaningfully to our strategic growth initiatives. This represents a slight decrease of approximately 3% compared to the $12.7 trillion spent in Q1 2024, but remains consistent with our projected full-year guidance of $48-50 trillion. It is also a 7% increase year-over-year compared to Q2 2023, reflecting our continued commitment to long-term growth and technological advancement, particularly in strategic areas.

Second, we saw positive contribution from wafer sales. While we saw robust demand overall, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors, our wafer sales experienced a mixed performance this quarter, primarily driven by the dynamics within the DRAM and NAND markets. Total wafer revenue increased by a modest 2% quarter-over-quarter to $8.7 billion. This growth was primarily fueled by increased production capacity and some strategic price adjustments.

And although still early, our sales by segment are showing promising trends. StellarTech's Q2 performance reveals a mixed bag, with strong performance in Memory and Mobile Panel offsetting sequential declines in MX and VD. System Semiconductors achieved record profitability, and Digital Appliances continued its impressive growth trajectory.

With that, I’ll turn it to David for a deeper look at operational performance.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was the foundry customer wins, particularly in emerging markets. Three of our design wins are with emerging smartphone manufacturers based in India and Southeast Asia, focusing on cost-effective, high-volume handsets. These wins are particularly valuable as they provide a strong foundation for future growth in these rapidly expanding markets. These customers are leveraging 3GAP for their application processors (APs) and power management integrated circuits (PMICs).

Additionally, improved inventory management has enabled more efficient production cycles. The DX business unit experienced the most significant inventory build-up, accounting for approximately 60% of the overall increase. This was primarily driven by strategic stockpiling of semiconductors, display panels, and specialized polymers, all vital for the production of our flagship product lines.

We’re also seeing early traction in our sales by segment, where updated processes and strategic initiatives are paying off. For example, Memory sales reached $18.5 billion in Q2, a 12% increase year-over-year (YoY) and a 7% increase quarter-over-quarter (QoQ). This growth was primarily driven by robust demand in the data center and enterprise server markets, alongside a surprising stability in Average Selling Prices (ASP).

Now I’ll pass it to Alicia for the tech and product update.

Alicia Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our proactive inventory strategy, supporting broader adoption and minimizing disruptions. We are investing in a new Advanced Inventory Management System (AIMS) that will provide real-time visibility into inventory levels across all business units and locations. AIMS will also incorporate advanced forecasting algorithms to improve demand planning and optimize inventory levels. We anticipate AIMS to be fully deployed by the end of Q3.

We’ve also support the enhanced performance of System Semiconductors, and our System Semiconductor revenue was $7.8 billion, a 15% increase YoY and a 9% increase QoQ. This growth was fueled by strong demand for advanced mobile processors and high-performance computing (HPC) solutions.

And finally, on sales by segment, our new architecture in Mobile Panels is driving growth. Mobile Panel achieved its highest-ever second-quarter revenue, reaching $9.2 billion, a 20% increase YoY and a 10% increase QoQ. This was driven by strong demand for premium OLED panels used in smartphones and tablets.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the revenue results and whether you expect this trend to continue?

Robert Maxwell:
Certainly. Our Q2 2024 consolidated revenue of $77.2 trillion exceeded the guidance of $74 trillion provided in the Q1 2024 earnings call. This outperformance reflects the company's ability to adapt to changing market conditions and execute its business strategy effectively. We are cautiously optimistic about the second half of the year, but macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical risks could impact our performance. We will continue to monitor the market closely and adjust our strategies as needed. We expect continued growth in the HBM market to significantly contribute to the DS division's revenue in the second half of 2024.

Analyst 2:
On CapEx, how much of the investment is specifically allocated to the Foundry business?

Susan Chen:
For the Foundry business, our CapEx investments are laser-focused on expanding our production capacity for advanced process nodes, specifically 5-nanometer and below. This includes both EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet) lithography equipment and the associated infrastructure. We've seen a significant increase in customer engagement for our 4nm and 3nm process technologies, particularly from companies designing high-performance computing (HPC) chips and AI accelerators. Specific numbers are proprietary, but it represents a substantial portion of the DS division's CapEx.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to the Advanced Inventory Management System?

Alicia Rodriguez:
The Advanced Inventory Management System (AIMS) is designed to provide real-time visibility into inventory levels across all business units and locations. AIMS will also incorporate advanced forecasting algorithms to improve demand planning and optimize inventory levels. We anticipate AIMS to be fully deployed by the end of Q3. This will allow us to optimize production scheduling, component substitution, and promotional activities.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on sales by segment, is this growth sustainable across all segments, or are there specific areas of concern?

David Lee:
While some segments experienced challenges, particularly the MX and VD businesses, the overall performance of StellarTech in Q2 was solid. The company's strategic focus on high-value products, technological innovation, and operational efficiency is expected to drive future growth. Macroeconomic headwinds, including inflation and supply chain disruptions, will continue to be closely monitored. We are confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are taking steps to address the sequential decline in earnings in the MX business by focusing on premium products, enhancing our customer experience, and optimizing our cost structure.

Closing

Robert Maxwell:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
